context: A small post office. Sachiko has come to mail a parcel to her son. Officer Takeda has stopped in on a routine visit and ends up holding the door.
purpose: tiny micro-courtesy — old woman, kind officer, no fuss

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: あら、ありがとうございます。
lines.style: Warm, proper gratitude. Slight formal bow in the voice—chin lowering just perceptibly. Soft attack, lingering on the thanks. Not rushed, completely present.

lines.speaker: takeda_officer
lines.style: Steady, measured professional kindness. Even tone, attentive gaze held in the voice. No hurry. Simple weight behind each word—the care underneath the courtesy.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お時間、本当に、すみません。
lines.en: Thank you—truly sorry to have taken your time.
lines.style: Soft, reflexive apology wrapped in genuine politeness. Slight hesitation before the second clause, as if checking herself. Trailing upward gently, not demanding reassurance.

lines.speaker: takeda_officer
lines.jp: 大丈夫ですよ。お荷物、お持ちしましょうか。
lines.en: Really? Oh, thank you—that's so kind of you.
lines.style: Small surprised lift on the opening. Warmth blooms across the sentence. Grateful, genuinely touched—not performing gratitude but feeling it. Voice opens up slightly.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 本当に？ありがとう、嬉しい。
lines.style: Warm pleasure mixed with surprise. Soft brightness in the tone. The delight is real but contained—elder's dignity held gently underneath the warmth.

lines.speaker: takeda_officer
lines.en: It was my pleasure. Please stay well.
lines.style: Genuine, unforced warmth. No performance in the sincerity. Steady closure—kind but not effusive. The voice carries quiet human connection, nothing more.
